q001.question: What are the main differences between evolutionary religion and revealed religion?
q001.answer: Evolutionary religion and revealed religion both deal with man's spiritual experience, but they show important differences in their origin and nature. The key difference lies in whether divine wisdom has directly intervened in human life. ● Evolutionary religion: a religion that arose and developed naturally, relying on human wisdom and experience. ○ On the basis of primitive fear, curiosity, anxiety, dreams, and the interpretation of natural phenomena, various forms of worship, magic, ritual, and a priestly class came into being. ○ Evolutionary religion appears in many different forms according to era and culture, but it is commonly based on a man-centered way of thinking. ○ The text acknowledges that even evolutionary religion, because it is a genuine experience, can possess loyalty and grandeur, but it judges that it offers a more limited spiritual vision than revealed religion. ○ The mention that Jesus was under the influence of evolutionary religion until his baptism shows the role of evolutionary religion as part of human experience. ● Revealed religion: a religion formed by the direct revelation of divine wisdom to man. ○ Revelation provides divine truth and insight that go beyond man's limited wisdom and opens a new path for man's spiritual growth. ○ The teachings and gospel of Jesus are the outstanding example of revealed religion. As the Son of God, Jesus revealed divine truth to man and taught such values as love, forgiveness, sacrifice, service, and eternal life. ○ The teachings of Melchizedek also belong to the category of revealed religion, and they influenced Abraham, Moses, Zoroaster, and others. ○ The text emphasizes that revealed religion is a form superior to evolutionary religion because divine wisdom is added to human wisdom. This makes possible an enlarged spiritual vision, higher levels of love and devotion, and a deeper understanding of the Fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man. In conclusion, evolutionary religion develops around human effort and experience, whereas revealed religion is formed through God's initiative, intervention, and revelation; this is where they differ. 100:6.7 (1101.2) ⟦P 100:6.7⟧ 100:6.8 (1101.3) ⟦P 100:6.8⟧ 100:6.9 (1101.4) ⟦P 100:6.9⟧ 100:7.1 (1101.5) ⟦P 100:7.1⟧

q002.question: What are the concepts of Deity, divinity, and God presented in The Urantia Book?
q002.answer:
The Urantia Book presents the concepts of Deity, divinity, and God in a highly complex and many-layered way. These three concepts are closely related to one another, yet they have subtle differences, and they must be understood in connection with such concepts as universe reality, personality, energy, and the Trinity.

1. Deity: diversity of existence and function. In the Urantia Papers, "Deity" means the ultimate source and unifier of universe reality. Deity may be a personal being, or it may exist in a state that transcends personality.[0:0.6~0:1.3] The Urantia Papers describe the functions of Deity on seven levels: ●Static level: self-contained and self-existent Deity. ●Potential level: self-willed and self-purposive Deity. ●Associative level: self-personalized and divinely fraternal Deity. ●Creative level: self-distributive and divinely revealed Deity. ●Evolutional level: self-expansive and creature-identified Deity. ●Supreme level: self-experiential and creature-Creator-unifying Deity. Deity functioning on the first creature-identificational level as time-space overcontroller of the grand universe; sometimes designated the Supremacy of Deity. ●Ultimate level: self-projected and time-space-transcending Deity. Deity omnipotent, omniscient, and omnipresent. Deity functioning on the second level of unifying divinity expression as effective overcontroller and absonite upholder of the master universe. [0:1.4~0:1.10] Through these diverse levels of function, Deity co-ordinates and unifies the whole universe.

2. Divinity: the attributes and characteristics of Deity. "Divinity" is the concept that designates the personality and attributes of Deity. Divinity means the perfect, unifying, and harmonious character of Deity. [0:4.3~6] The Urantia Book explains that divinity can be understood as truth, beauty, goodness, love, mercy, ministry, justice, power, sovereignty, and so on. [0:4.9~11] Depending on the level and manner of its existence, divinity may be perfect or imperfect, and it may also be relative. [0:4.13~0:5.2] For example, the divinity of Paradise is perfect, but the divinity of creatures evolving in time and space is imperfect.

3. God: the personalized concept of Deity. "God" is the term the Urantia Papers use to designate personalized Deity. [0:1.12~ 0:2.2] God includes various Deity personalities such as the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit.

Depending on the context, God may designate a particular Deity personality, or may indicate a level of Deity or a degree of association. For example, "God the Father" designates the person of the Universal Father, whereas "God the Supreme" means Deity evolving in time and space.

4. The interrelationship of Deity, divinity, and God. In the Urantia Papers, Deity is the source of divinity, and divinity expresses the characteristics of Deity. God is the personalized form of Deity, possesses divinity, and carries out the will of Deity. In the Urantia Papers, Deity, divinity, and God are closely interrelated, and they are also connected with such concepts as universe reality, personality, energy, and the Trinity, bearing complex and many-layered meanings. Understanding these concepts comprehensively plays an important role in grasping the central message of the Urantia Papers. (Reference passages) 0:1.1 The universe of universes presents phenomena of deity activities on diverse levels of cosmic realities, mind meanings, and spirit values, but all of these ministrations—personal or otherwise—are divinely co-ordinated. 0:1.2 DEITY is personalizable as God, is prepersonal and superpersonal in ways not altogether comprehensible by man. Deity is characterized by the quality of unity—actual or potential—on all supermaterial levels of reality; and this unifying quality is best comprehended by creatures as divinity.

q003.question: What is the difference between the Unqualified Absolute and the Universal Father?
q003.answer: The Unqualified Absolute and the Universal Father both represent fundamental aspects of universe reality, but there are important differences in their attributes and functions. ●The Universal Father (God) is the personal expression of the First Source and Center, the source of all creation and the ultimate controller of all reality. [0:3.9~11] ○The Universal Father is personal; he is Creator, Controller, and Upholder.[0:2.3~0:2.9] ○The Universal Father is the center of moral beings and of potential personality. ●The Unqualified Absolute, on the other hand, is an impersonal, extradivine, and undeified reality. [0:11.6~8] ○The Unqualified Absolute has no personality, divinity, or creator prerogatives. ○The Unqualified Absolute is contrasted with the Deity Absolute, the potential segregated from infinite total reality by the free will of the Universal Father. ○The Unqualified Absolute is a universal physical force, but it is conditioned by life, mind, spirit, personality, will, response, and the will of the Paradise Trinity. [0:11.10~12] The Deity Absolute is the realm in which the creative activities of the Universal Father take place, while the Unqualified Absolute is potential existing outside the range of such activities. The two Absolutes are perfectly unified in the Universal Absolute. [0:11.13~15] In conclusion, the Universal Father, as the personal God, presides over and upholds all creation, whereas the Unqualified Absolute, as an impersonal reality, transcends the realms of divinity and creation. 0:3.9 God, as the First Source and Center, is primal in relation to total reality—unqualifiedly. The First Source and Center is infinite as well as eternal and is therefore limited or conditioned only by volition. 0:3.10 God—the Universal Father—is the personality of the First Source and Center and as such maintains personal relations of infinite control over all co-ordinate and subordinate sources and centers. Such control is personal and infinite in potential, even though it may never actually function owing to the perfection of the function of such co-ordinate and subordinate sources and centers and personalities. 0:3.11 The First Source and Center is, therefore, primal in all domains: deified or undeified, personal or impersonal, actual or potential, finite or infinite. No thing or being, no relativity or finality, exists except in direct or indirect relation to, and dependence on, the primacy of the First Source and Center.

q004.question: What elements are essential to man's religious growth?
q004.answer: Various elements work together as essentials in man's religious growth. Looking at the main elements presented in The Urantia Book, they are as follows. ●Spiritual insight: The heart of religious growth lies in communion with divinity, not through emotions or feelings, but through spiritually elevated thinking. The divine nature can be perceived only with the eyes of the mind, and only through a pure mind can one truly discern God and hear the voice of the indwelling Adjuster. In other words, religious experience does not mean simply following the object of belief blindly; it means insight gained through deep thinking and spiritual striving. 101:1.3 The divine spirit makes contact with mortal man, not by feelings or emotions, but in the realm of the highest and most spiritualized thinking. It is your thoughts, not your feelings, that lead you Godward. The divine nature may be perceived only with the eyes of the mind. But the mind that really discerns God, hears the indwelling Adjuster, is the pure mind. "⟦Q 101:1.3⟧“Sem consagrar-se, nenhum homem pode ver o Senhor.”⟦/Q⟧." All such inner and spiritual communion is termed spiritual insight. Such religious experiences result from the impress made upon the mind of man by the combined operations of the Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth as they function amid and upon the ideas, ideals, insights, and spirit strivings of the evolving sons of God. 101:1.4 Religion lives and prospers, then, not by sight and feeling, but rather by faith and insight. It consists not in the discovery of new facts or in the finding of a unique experience, but rather in the discovery of new and spiritual meanings in facts already well known to mankind. The highest religious experience is not dependent on prior acts of belief, tradition, and authority; neither is religion the offspring of sublime feelings and purely mystical emotions. It is, rather, a profoundly deep and actual experience of spiritual communion with the spirit influences resident within the human mind, and as far as such an experience is definable in terms of psychology, it is simply the experience of experiencing the reality of believing in God as the reality of such a purely personal experience. ●Faith: Religion is not mere knowledge or assent to doctrine; it is a dynamic power that lives and breathes through faith in, and insight into, the unseen realm. Faith is the driving force that enables man to face the vicissitudes of life bravely, and it provides the impetus that keeps him moving forward unceasingly. 102:2.8 Again, there are other types of unstable and poorly disciplined souls who would use the sentimental ideas of religion as an avenue of escape from the irritating demands of living. When certain vacillating and timid mortals attempt to escape from the incessant pressure of evolutionary life, religion, as they conceive it, seems to present the nearest refuge, the best avenue of escape. But it is the mission of religion to prepare man for bravely, even heroically, facing the vicissitudes of life. Religion is evolutionary man's supreme endowment, the one thing which enables him to carry on and "⟦Q 102:2.8⟧endure as seeing Him who is invisible⟦/Q⟧." Mysticism, however, is often something of a retreat from life which is embraced by those humans who do not relish the more robust activities of living a religious life in the open arenas of human society and commerce. True religion must act. Conduct will be the result of religion when man actually has it, or rather when religion is permitted truly to possess the man. Never will religion be content with mere thinking or unacting feeling. ●Action: True religion must go beyond thought and belief and lead to actual conduct. Religious conviction can at times be distorted and bring about negative results, but in its essence it is dynamic and possesses a power that leads one constantly to do something. ● Revelation: Man can surmise the existence of God through nature as well, but revelation is needed in order to meet a personal God fully. Revelation appears periodically as an epochal phenomenon, but on the personal level it takes place continuously. The Thought Adjuster of the divine Father, the Spirit of Truth of the Son, and the Holy Spirit of the Universe Spirit work unceasingly within man, carrying out the supreme ministry that is unified through the evolution of human experience. 101:2.11 The contemplation of nature does logically point in the direction of intelligent guidance, even living supervision, but it does not in any satisfactory manner reveal a personal God. On the other hand, nature discloses nothing which would preclude the universe from being looked upon as the handiwork of the God of religion. God cannot be found through nature alone, but man having otherwise found him, the study of nature becomes wholly consistent with a higher and more spiritual interpretation of the universe. 101:2.12 Revelation as an epochal phenomenon is periodic; as a personal human experience it is continuous. Divinity functions in mortal personality as the Adjuster gift of the Father, as the Spirit of Truth of the Son, and as the Holy Spirit of the Universe Spirit, while these three supermortal endowments are unified in human experiential evolution as the ministry of the Supreme.

q005.question: How does the Paradise Trinity differ from the post-Havona Trinities?
q005.answer:
1. The Paradise Trinity. The Paradise Trinity is the existential Trinity composed of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit. Since the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit coexist eternally with the Universal Father, they exist beyond time and space. The Paradise Trinity is the ultimate source of all reality and personality, and the fundamental driving force of all creation and administration in the universe. ●The Universal Father: the source and father of all reality. He possesses an infinite, eternal, and absolute personality. ●The Eternal Son: the Son born of the perfect first thought of the Universal Father. He perfectly reveals the personal nature of the Father and experiences the fullness of the divine personalities. ●The Infinite Spirit: the conjoint personality who appears as the result of the united action of the Universal Father and the Eternal Son. He represents the united nature of the Universal Father and the Eternal Son and acts as the universal minister of mercy.

2. The post-Havona Trinities. Unlike the Paradise Trinity, the post-Havona Trinities are experiential Trinities. That is, they are composed of beings who evolve and grow in time and space, and they are formed through the experiential actualization of realities created by the Paradise Trinity. The post-Havona Trinities are divided into two. ●The Ultimate Trinity: includes the Supreme Being, the Supreme Creator Personalities, and the absonite Architects of the Master Universe. The Ultimate Trinity is formed through the eternal fusion of the finite and the infinite, and it gains power and becomes personalized in the expanding realms of the master universe. ●The Absolute Trinity: composed of God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and the unrevealed Consummator of Universe Destiny. This Trinity functions on personal and superpersonal levels, and it extends its influence even to the borders of the nonpersonal.

3. The differences between the Paradise Trinity and the post-Havona Trinities. ●Existential vs. experiential: The Paradise Trinity is an existential Trinity that exists from eternity, whereas the post-Havona Trinities are experiential Trinities that evolve in time and space. ●Infinite vs. finite: The Paradise Trinity possesses infinite divinity, but the post-Havona Trinities are composed of derived Deities and are not infinite. ●Source of creation vs. result of creation: The Paradise Trinity is the source of all creation, whereas the post-Havona Trinities appear as the result of the creative acts of the Paradise Trinity.

4. Conclusion. The Paradise Trinity is the fundamental driving force of the universe and the ultimate source of all reality and personality. The post-Havona Trinities are composed of beings who evolve in time and space, and they reveal their divinity through the creative acts of the Paradise Trinity. The two kinds of Trinity have different characteristics, but they are related in co-operating for the harmony and completion of the universe.

q006.question: What were the purpose and meaning of Michael's bestowal on Urantia?
q006.answer:
Michael, that is, Jesus, came down to Urantia in what is regarded as one of the most important events in human history. His coming was not a mere visit but an event of universal significance. The purpose and meaning of Michael's coming to Urantia can be summarized as follows.

1. Ending the rebellion and establishing sovereignty. Michael's most important purpose was to bring an end to the confusion caused by the Lucifer rebellion and the Caligastia betrayal, and to establish his sovereignty in the universe of Nebadon. This meant more than simply regaining power. He sought to restore universe order through the harmony of mercy and justice. Because Urantia was a center of this rebellion, Michael intervened directly here in the form of the lowest of creatures, confronting and triumphing over the forces of evil, and thereby firmly established his authority throughout the whole universe.

2. Love and service for Urantia. Michael had a deep love for, and sense of responsibility toward, Urantia. He sought to comfort and heal the Urantians who were suffering because of the Caligastia betrayal and the Adamic default. He also showed Urantians the love of God the Father and led them to realize that they are children of God. In particular, he emphasized that his mission was to reveal the Father in human life, so that those who seek God might see the Father.

3. The coming of a new spiritual age. Michael's bestowal meant more than simply correcting past wrongs. His life and teachings were the signal announcing the beginning of a new spiritual age. He proclaimed a gospel of love and mercy that went beyond the law, and he emphasized man's inner transformation and spiritual growth. He taught men to seek spiritual truth through a direct relationship with God the Father, not bound by old religious forms and traditions. The meaning of Michael's bestowal: Michael's bestowal on Urantia signifies the triumph of justice and mercy on a universal scale, and to Urantia it brought the dawn of a new spiritual age and the realization of the love of God the Father. His teachings continue to have a great influence on mankind even today, and through his life we learn the meaning of true love, service, and spiritual growth. 120:2.2 "2. Apart from your earth mission and your universe revelation, but incidental to both, I counsel that you assume, after you are sufficiently self-conscious of your divine identity, the additional task of technically terminating the Lucifer rebellion in the system of Satania, and that you do all this as the Son of Man; thus, as a mortal creature of the realm, in weakness made powerful by faith-submission to the will of your Father, I suggest that you graciously achieve all you have repeatedly declined arbitrarily to accomplish by power and might when you were so endowed at the time of the inception of this sinful and unjustified rebellion. I would regard it as a fitting climax of your mortal bestowal if you should return to us as the Son of Man, Planetary Prince of Urantia, as well as the Son of God, supreme sovereign of your universe. As a mortal man, the lowest type of intelligent creature in Nebadon, meet and adjudicate the blasphemous pretensions of Caligastia and Lucifer and, in your assumed humble estate, forever end the shameful misrepresentations of these fallen children of light. Having steadfastly declined to discredit these rebels through the exercise of your creator prerogatives, now it would be fitting that you should, in the likeness of the lowest creatures of your creation, wrest dominion from the hands of these fallen Sons; and so would your whole local universe in all fairness clearly and forever recognize the justice of your doing in the role of mortal flesh those things which mercy admonished you not to do by the power of arbitrary authority. And having thus by your bestowal established the possibility of the sovereignty of the Supreme in Nebadon, you will in effect have brought to a close the unadjudicated affairs of all preceding insurrections, notwithstanding the greater or lesser time lag involved in the realization of this achievement. By this act the pending dissensions of your universe will be in substance liquidated. And with the subsequent endowment of supreme sovereignty over your universe, similar challenges to your authority can never recur in any part of your great personal creation. 120:2.3 "3. When you have succeeded in terminating the Urantia secession, as you undoubtedly will, I counsel you to accept from Gabriel the conference of the title of 'Planetary Prince of Urantia' as the eternal recognition by your universe of your final bestowal experience; and that you further do any and all things, consistent with the purport of your bestowal, to atone for the sorrow and confusion brought upon Urantia by the Caligastia betrayal and the subsequent Adamic default.

q007.question: Definitions and key content of the concepts of Deity and divinity
q007.answer:
1. Definitions and key content of the concepts of Deity and divinity. Definitions of Deity and divinity. **Deity** is the source of all existence and the ultimate reality; it is infinite and eternal, and it differentiates itself through free will. Deity is manifested in divine personalities such as the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit, who are together called the **Paradise Trinity**. Divinity: the characteristic of Deity that expresses its nature, the unifying and co-ordinating quality of Deity. To creatures it is comprehensible as truth, beauty, and goodness; in relation to personality it is understood as love, mercy, and ministry; and on impersonal levels it is disclosed as justice, power, and sovereignty. God: the word designating personalized Deity; depending on the context, it may designate the person of the Universal Father. God always refers to personality, whereas Deity may or may not refer to personality. Key theological content (the levels and functions of divinity). Deity is not a single static being; it can function on seven levels, from the finite to the absolute, which shows that the universe is not a static perfection but an evolving experiential reality. The Universal Father (the First Source and Center): the foundation of all reality, an infinite and eternal personality. The Father sends **his pure fragment of Deity, the Thought Adjuster**, to indwell the human mind, in order to help the evolution of the immortal soul for man's eternal survival. Trinitarian differentiation and association: The Universal Father achieved threefold Deity personalization through the appearance of the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit, and this enabled the Father to escape the diffusion of his potentials through unified Deity. The evolution of experiential Deity: In addition to the existential Paradise Deities (Father, Son, and Spirit), experiential Deities such as God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and **God the Absolute** are evolving.

God the Supreme: Deity actualizing and evolving in time and space, the personal God who experientially achieves the unification of creature and Creator. Divine attributes (love, justice, mercy): God is spirit and God is love. Divine justice is tempered by mercy, and mercy is justice tempered by perfect knowledge and by recognition of the natural weaknesses of finite creatures. God's love is by nature a fatherly affection.

2. Definition and key content of the concept of spirit. Definition of spirit. **Spirit** is one of the fundamental dimensions of universe reality, related to the highest reality of divinity and personality. Spirit: the ultimate reality of the personal universe, the highest personal reality of finite creation. It is also a symbolic expression denoting the characteristic by which various orders of spiritual beings, including the spirit of God indwelling the human mind (the Thought Adjuster), are manifested as personalities. The function of spirit in personality: Spirit is the soul of creation, contrasted with the shadow of matter, the physical body. Mind mediates between spirit and matter in personality. Universal spirit activity and its philosophical significance. Spirit plays a central role in the creature ascension plan and in the ministry of Deity. The Infinite Spirit and spiritual ministry: **The Infinite Spirit** is the executive agent of the united thought and the unified word of the Father and the Son, the bestower of mind and the minister of mercy. Guidance on the ascending path: The technique of mortal survival lies in the gradual transformation of the God-conscious mind of the human will into a mind that is increasingly spirit-taught and ultimately spirit-led. The spirit offspring of the Infinite Spirit are devoted to ministering the love of God and the mercy of the Son to all intelligent creatures of the evolutionary worlds, and they constitute the living ladder that ascends from chaos to glory. The answering of prayer: Spiritual gravity (centered in the Eternal Son) is the actual existence of spiritual values and spiritual forces, and only when a human petition has spiritual content does it ascend by this spirit circuit and become effective.

3. Definition and key content of the concepts of matter and energy.

Definition of matter and energy. The sources understand material reality as various forms of energy, and these are controlled by physical gravity. Energy: used as a term embracing everything in the spiritual, mindal, and material realms. Physical energy: denotes all phases and forms of phenomenal motion, action, and potential. The Isle of Paradise: the source and center of physical bodies and the absolute pattern of the material reality of the universe. The Isle of Paradise is the absolute that controls the material gravity of the First Source and Center. The stages of matter: Physical energy appears in three stages: space potency or force (derived from the Unqualified Absolute, not responsive to Paradise gravity), emergent energy (responsive to Paradise gravity), and **universe power (directly responsive to linear gravity)**. Key cosmo-philosophical content (the control and limits of matter). The source of matter: All original force-energy proceeds from Paradise, and all physical energy and other material manifestations derive from the activity of the Universal Father. The role of gravity: Gravity alone controls energy-matter. All creation revolves eternally around the Paradise-personality center, and the gravity forces of the material universe converge in the gravity center of nether Paradise. Relation to the spiritual universe: The material universe is always the arena in which all spiritual activities take place; spirit beings and ascenders live and work on physical spheres of material reality. Matter, mind, and spirit are equally real, but in personality spirit is striving for mastery through the mediation of mind. The limits and evolution of matter: Reality as measured by response to material gravity is the antithesis of reality as determined by quality of spirit content. The more spiritual a mind becomes, the less responsive it is to material gravity; and the material creation is not a part of Deity but only a consequence.

4. The cosmic philosophy and revelation unifying the three concepts. The three reality concepts of Deity, spirit, and matter interact and are unified through the concepts of **personality** and **mind**. The role of mind: Mind mediates between spirit and matter. Mind is meaning, energy is thing, and spirit is value. **The Conjoint Actor (the Infinite Spirit)** is absolute in the domain of mind, and the bestowal of mind is a universal ministry to beings that represents the unification of both the material and the spiritual creation.

The unification of personality: Personality is a level of deified reality, and personality is the gift of the Paradise Father. As this personality unifies matter and spirit through the mediation of mind, the immortal soul evolves. Ultimately, personality can reach the state in which God and man can exist as one unified personality (for example, Christ Michael). This revelation declares that the universe is not mechanically or passively perfect but is a personal and progressive creation. Disharmony and misunderstanding are possible, but these are evidence of the existence and acts of personality, and they provide opportunity for the growth, experience, and adventure of personality. Man's ultimate destiny is to attain the perfection of God through this spiritual progress and experience.

q008.question: The location of Urantia within the vast structure of the universe
q008.answer:
1. The location of Urantia within the vast structure of the universe. Urantia is one inhabited planet within the vast reality called the universe of universes, and its location has the following hierarchical structure. Urantia: "⟦Q 0:0.5⟧one of many similar inhabited planets which comprise the local universe of Nebadon⟦/Q⟧." The local universe of Nebadon: This local universe, made up of numerous inhabited planets, is part of the superuniverse of Orvonton. The superuniverse of Orvonton: Nebadon together with other similar creations makes up this superuniverse, and Orvonton is one of the seven superuniverses evolving in time and space. Orvonton has Uversa as its capital. The central universe of Havona: These seven evolving superuniverses revolve around Havona, the central universe, a perfect divine creation without beginning or end. The Isle of Paradise: At the heart of the eternal central universe of Havona is the stationary Isle of Paradise, the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of the eternal God (the Universal Father). Paradise is the universal headquarters of all personality activities and the source and center of all force-space and energy manifestations. The grand universe: The central divine universe (Havona) and these seven superuniverses together are called the grand universe. This grand universe is the universe that is now organized and inhabited and is being further organized. In summary, Urantia is one of the countless worlds located in the evolving outer domain of the grand universe, and it belongs to Orvonton, the seventh superuniverse, outward from Paradise, the ultimate goal.

2. The role of the mortal ascension plan. The mortal ascension plan is the universal and eternal purpose designed so that man, a finite creature, may ultimately attain divine perfection, enter into relationship with the infinite God, and take part in universe service. The ultimate goal and destiny. The key roles and goals of the mortal ascension plan are as follows. Attainment of divine perfection: The Universal Father has set a high and divine goal for finite man, and the attainment of the perfection of God is the final and certain destiny of man's eternal spiritual progression.

The journey of finding God: This exalted quest for the God of universes is the supreme adventure of the inhabitants of all the worlds of time and space. The end of this journey is that material creatures achieve spiritual transformation and ultimately stand in the presence of God on Paradise. Joining the Corps of the Finality: The mortal who fuses with the Adjuster receives the divine certification of eventual Paradise attainment, and every mortal who knows God and attains Paradise is destined to be mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality. They will embark upon unknown universe adventures exploring the infinity of the Universal Father. The mechanism of executing the ascension plan and its existential significance. This plan is carried out by the united efforts and functions of the Paradise Deities (the Trinity). The bestowal of the Universal Father: The Universal Father sends **his pure fragment of Deity, the Thought Adjuster**, to indwell the human mind, in order to help the evolution of the immortal soul for man's eternal survival. This Adjuster helps the human mind to grasp spiritual values and true universe meanings. The sponsorship of the Eternal Son (the plan of attainment): The Eternal Son is eternally associated with the Father in the successful execution of the divine plan for the creation, evolution, ascension, and perfection of will creatures. The Eternal Son is the personal trustee and divine custodian of the creature ascension plan. The bestowal and role of the Creator Sons: The Creator Sons of the local universes provide the way whereby finite man can become immortal and be embraced in the bosom of infinity. In particular, on Urantia, through the bestowal of the Creator Son Michael (Jesus), the nature and personality of God were revealed in human experience, and thereby the Paradise plan of mortal survival was enhanced and illuminated. The Creator Son functions as a rescuer who restores the spiritual status of the spheres when rebellion occurs. The ministry of the Infinite Spirit (the ministry of mercy): The Infinite Spirit plans and executes the tremendous universe scheme of mercy ministry that is essential to the practical and effective operation of the attainment and bestowal enterprises of the Father and the Son. The spirit offspring of the Infinite Spirit are devoted to ministering the love of God and the mercy of the Son to all intelligent creatures of the evolutionary worlds, and these spirit beings constitute the living ladder that ascends from chaos to glory. Universe significance (the justification of evolution): The evolutionary universes, including Urantia, are not mechanically perfect, and disharmony and misunderstanding are possible; but these are evidence of the existence and acts of personality in the universe, and they provide opportunity for the growth, experience, and adventure of personality. The mortal ascension plan is the very core that justifies this personal and progressive creation of the universe. The particular situation of Urantia (failure and challenge).

Urantia has suffered difficulties arising from the Lucifer rebellion and the Caligastia betrayal, and the failure of Adam and Eve was a deviation from the divine plan; yet in spite of all these challenges mankind has been greatly uplifted, and their ascension plan is still actively going forward. On this planet every facility and every power have been provided to assure the eventual achievement of the Paradise goal of mortals, the attainment of divine perfection. Figurative understanding: The mortal ascension plan is like the curriculum of a school. Urantia (an evolutionary planet) corresponds to the classroom of the lowest grade in this education, and the students (mortals) grow with the help of the indwelling teacher (the Thought Adjuster). They pass their examinations (experiences) and, by way of the local universe (the upper grades) and Havona (the university course), they reach the ultimate goal, Paradise (the highest school). This whole course is a plan reflecting the love and educational zeal of the Universal Father, so that the students may finally graduate and become final universe servants carrying out the eternal purpose of the universe.

q009.question: How did the death of Joseph, the father of Jesus, affect Jesus?
q009.answer: The death of Joseph had a great influence on the life of Jesus. **First of all, it brought economic hardship.** Before Joseph died, Jesus' family was economically secure, and Jesus was soon to go to Jerusalem to study with the rabbis. But because of Joseph's death, Jesus gave up studying in Jerusalem and became the head of the household, responsible for supporting the family. **After Joseph's death the family's financial situation grew rapidly worse.** In the year he turned fifteen, Jesus devoted himself to carpentry work to support the family, but before long the savings ran out, and things came to the point where they had to sell the house. To pay the taxes they had to sell the harp, and the tax collectors even threatened to seize the harp in order to extract more taxes from Jesus. He went to Sepphoris to collect the money due from Herod at the time of Joseph's death, but Herod ruled that nothing could be paid, which was a great disappointment to Jesus. **Second, Joseph's death awakened in Jesus a sense of responsibility and maturity.** Having become head of the family at the young age of fourteen, Jesus worked devotedly for the family and played the role of a father, teaching and caring for his younger brothers and sisters. He came through the difficulties with a positive and realistic attitude, and he inspired hope and courage in the family. **Finally, Joseph's death became an occasion for Jesus to think more deeply about his destiny and mission.** Had Joseph lived, Jesus would have studied in Jerusalem to become a rabbi, but because of Joseph's death he was placed in a situation where he had to decide the direction of his life for himself. He realized that he was not the Messiah the Jews expected, and he chose the title "Son of Man." Also, even amid his responsibility of caring for the family, he prepared for his mission and strove to follow the will of the Father in heaven. In conclusion, Joseph's death was a great trial for Jesus, but at the same time it was an important event that matured him as a man and led him onward toward his mission.

q010.question: What are the essence and the various attributes of the concept of God presented in The Urantia Book?
q010.answer:
The Urantia Book describes God as the source of all reality and as the ultimate reality. God is the primal reality of the spiritual world, the source of truth in the realm of mind, and the One whose presence extends throughout the whole material realm. To all mind creatures God is a personality, and to the universe as a whole he is the First Source and Center of eternal reality. The essence and various attributes of God presented in The Urantia Book are as follows.

1. The essence of God. 1) Spiritual reality: God is the source of the spiritual world, a universal spiritual presence. Man is the offspring of God and was created in the image of God, but one must not think that God has a form and appearance like man's. 2) Personality: God is a **personal being**, not merely a concept or a law. He is beyond man's highest longings and searchings, and he is not a psychological object projected by the human mind. As the Universal Father, God is the acme of divine personality, and throughout all creation he is the origin and destiny of personality. 3) Transcendence: God is an infinite and eternal being who transcends human understanding. His thoughts and plans are unsearchable, and his greatness is immeasurable.

2. The attributes of God. 1) Love and mercy: God is a being full of love and mercy. He shows divine kindness to sinners and receives in mercy those who return to righteousness. The greatest proof of this is the indwelling Adjuster, the gift of God. 2) Omnipotence: God is the all-powerful being who controls all power and has made all energy circuits. He determines the time and manner of all forms of energy and material manifestation, and he holds all these perpetually within his control. 3) Omniscience: God has an infinite and all-knowing mind. Even as the universe grows and the beings within it increase, the wisdom of God is not diminished. His act of sending his spirit messengers to his creatures does not limit his abilities, and there is no limit to the number of such spirit observers. 4) Goodness: God is good, divine, and gracious. The goodness of God shows that the universe is intelligent and is a managed personality. That human personality can experience the universe means that a divine mind and a potential personality exist.

3. The relationship between God and man. 1) The indwelling Adjuster: God communicates with man through the Adjuster indwelling the human mind. The Adjuster is a fragment of God that helps man receive spiritual guidance and experience the presence of God. 2) Spiritual evolution: Man evolves spiritually according to God's plan, with the ultimate goal of becoming one with God. God's plan includes the creation, evolution, ascension, and perfection of will creatures. 3) Sonship with God: Man is a son of God, and within the family of divine sonship he can realize his place and achieve the Paradise goal of attaining the perfection of God. The Urantia Book presents the concept of God from various aspects, seeking to help man understand God and develop his relationship with God.

q011.question: What is the structure of the universe described in The Urantia Book, and what is the role of God within it?
q011.answer:
The Urantia Book describes a vast universe structure centered on God, and within it God performs various roles.

1. The structure of the universe. 1) The seven superuniverses: the seven enormous universe domains surrounding the central universe. 2) The central universe: an eternal and perfect universe that includes Paradise and Havona. 3) The local universes: universes created and administered by the Creator Sons; Urantia belongs to the local universe called Nebadon.

2. The nature of God. 1)The First Source and Center: the being who is the foundation of all reality, eternal and infinite. God, the Universal Father, is the personality of the First Source and Center and maintains infinite control over all other sources and centers. 2) The Eternal Son: the being who came forth from the first perfect and infinite thought of the First Source and Center; he fully reveals the divine personalities. 3) The Infinite Spirit: the perfect creative concept for the conjoint action of the First Source and Center and the Eternal Son, the full and unique revelation of the Universal Father and the Eternal Son. 4) The Paradise Trinity: the perfect union of the First Source and Center, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit, eternal and potentially infinite. 5) The post-Havona Trinities: Trinities composed of derived Deities, namely the Ultimate Trinity and the Absolute Trinity. These evolve through the experiential actualization of realities created by the Paradise Trinity. 6) The Supreme Being: the being who is being actualized in the evolving universes, the co-ordinator of Deity activities and the synthesizer of the experiential unification of Trinity Deity in time and space. 7) God the Ultimate: the personal Deity functioning on absonite divinity levels and in the time-space-transcending universe; he transcends the Supreme Being and is eventuated. 8) God the Absolute: Deity existing in the unity of the Absolute Trinity.

3. The role of God. The role of God as described in The Urantia Book is as follows. 1) Creator: God is the creator of all universes and of all beings within them. 2) Controller: God is the primal cause of all universe energy and material phenomena, and he holds everything within his gravity control. 3) Upholder: God upholds and preserves all creation, and his power and energy circulate throughout the whole universe. 4) Father: God is the Father of all personal beings, and to man in particular he is a loving and merciful Father. 5) Revealer: God reveals himself through the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit, and he indwells man through the Thought Adjuster. 6) Perfecter: God guides his creatures to evolve and progress toward perfection, and in the end he desires to become one with them. While acknowledging that man, with his finite understanding, cannot fully grasp the infinity of God, The Urantia Book emphasizes that through faith, worship, and service one can develop a relationship with God and achieve spiritual growth.

q012.question: What is the process of man's spiritual evolution as explained in The Urantia Book, and what is its meaning?
q012.answer: The Urantia Book describes the process of man's spiritual evolution as an ascent from material existence toward spiritual perfection. Man is a spiritual being dwelling in a physical body, and within him dwells a fragment of God called the Thought Adjuster. This Adjuster guides man spiritually and makes connection with God possible. Man's spiritual evolution is the process of changing from a material mind to a spiritual mind. The material mind bound to the physical body perishes with death, but the mind connected with spirit creates a soul, and this soul is immortal and goes on to eternal life. This change is made possible through the guidance of the Thought Adjuster together with the individual's will and God-conscious effort. When man submits to the spiritual leading of the Adjuster and pursues spiritual values, the material mind is gradually spiritualized and creates an immortal entity called the soul. The soul continues to grow in the spiritual world beyond the material world, and ultimately it fuses with spirit, becomes a spirit being, and reaches Paradise, where the Universal Father dwells. The Urantia Book calls this process the plan of progressive attainment, an eternal journey in which all beings created according to the will of the Universal Father take part. This plan shows the love and mercy of God, who grants man the prerogative of personality and helps him achieve divine perfection through unceasing ascent. Man's spiritual evolution goes beyond mere individual perfection; it is connected with the evolution of the whole universe. The Urantia Book explains that all beings are guided by the evolving Deity called the Supreme Being and are moving toward the eternal fusion of the finite and the infinite. This shows that human life and choices have universal meaning and that all of us are participating in the realization of eternal divinity. In the end, the spiritual evolution presented by The Urantia Book is an ascent from material existence toward spiritual perfection, a majestic plan that goes beyond individual growth and is connected with the evolution of the whole universe. It is a divine prerogative given to man, an eternal journey made possible through unceasing effort and the grace of God.

q013.question: How is the difference between finite reality and absonite reality explained?
q013.answer:
The Urantia Book distinguishes finite reality and absonite reality in three respects: origin, relation to time and space, and relation to Deity.

1. Origin: Finite reality is created existence and necessarily has a beginning. Absonite reality, on the other hand, is not created but self-originated existence, without beginning or end. That is, finite reality was created by Deity, whereas absonite reality is existence that has been with Deity from eternity.

2. Relation to time and space: Finite reality is existence subject to the limitations of time and space. This means all beings of the material world, including man, who lives a finite life. Absonite reality, by contrast, transcends time and space and belongs to the domain of eternal and infinite existence.

3. Relation to Deity: Finite reality is related to the Supremacy of Deity. The Supremacy of Deity signifies the role of the Creator who creates and cares for finite beings. Absonite reality, on the other hand, is related to the Ultimacy of Deity. The Ultimacy of Deity signifies the state of Deity that is related to absonite realities in the domain that transcends time and space. Although The Urantia Book thus distinguishes finite reality from absonite reality, it explains that ultimately all reality derives from the source of Deity. God, the First Source and Center, is the foundation of all reality, and both finite and absonite realities are contained within the infinite potential of Deity. In the end, The Urantia Book offers the hope that even finite man can, through unceasing spiritual evolution, progress toward absonite existence. Man has within him the Thought Adjuster, a fragment of God, and through it he is connected with God. When man achieves spiritual growth by following the leading of the Adjuster, he can go beyond the limitations of finite existence and draw nearer to the infinity of God.

q014.question: Explain the various ways of understanding divinity in three dimensions.
q014.answer: The Urantia Book presents various ways of understanding divinity and explains them in three dimensions: origin, function, and relationship. First, from the standpoint of origin, divinity is divided into existential divinity, experiential divinity, and derived divinity. Existential divinity means the absolute and infinite divinity that exists from eternity, embodied in the Paradise Trinity. The Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit are the primal divinity, uncreated and self-existent, without beginning or end. Experiential divinity, on the other hand, means divinity that evolves and grows in time and space. The Supreme Being, God the Ultimate, and others are divinity that starts from the potential of existential divinity and develops continually through the experience and interaction of finite creatures. Finally, derived divinity means the divine personalities that proceed from existential divinity. The Creator Sons, the Ancients of Days, the Seven Master Spirits, the Thought Adjusters, and others are beings derived in order to carry out the will and purpose of God, and each reflects divinity through its assigned role and function. Second, from the standpoint of function, divinity performs five roles: creation, control, evolution, revelation, and love and mercy. Divinity is the source of all existence and the power that creates and upholds the material universe, the spiritual world, and the realm of mind. It also maintains the order and harmony of the universe and governs the interaction of all realities through laws and principles. Divinity leads all beings toward perfection and helps finite creatures participate in divinity through spiritual growth. It also discloses its nature and will in various ways, guiding man so that he may understand and experience God. Finally, divinity loves all creatures unconditionally and, in spite of their errors and failures, opens the way of forgiveness and salvation. Third, from the standpoint of relationship, divinity is explained in terms of the Trinity relationship, the relationship with creatures, and spiritual evolution. Divinity appears through the perfect union of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit, and these three persons are interdependent and complete one another. Divinity is also connected with all creatures, and through the Thought Adjuster it directly indwells the human mind and enters into a personal relationship. Through his relationship with divinity, man can grow spiritually and participate in the nature of God, with the ultimate goal of becoming one with God. In conclusion, The Urantia Book presents divinity not as a single, fixed concept but as a dynamic reality with various dimensions. By exploring and understanding the various aspects of divinity, man can realize his spiritual potential and live a richer life.

q015.question: What relationship does the First Source and Center have with the universe?
q015.answer: The First Source and Center is the source and upholder of all reality, and the universe is the creation of that First Source and Center. The First Source and Center is personalized as the Universal Father, and the universe is the result of that Father's thought and action. To explain in more detail, the First Source and Center relates to the universe in the following ways. ● Source of creation: The First Source and Center is the source of all universe energy and matter, and the universe was created from that force and energy. All creation revolves around Paradise, the First Source and Center, and is held by the gravity of Paradise. ● Control and co-ordination: As the Universal Father, the First Source and Center controls and co-ordinates everything in the universe and maintains its order and harmony through universe law. Although the Universal Father does not make direct contact with every creature, he exerts his influence in the universe through his personality circuit and the Thought Adjusters. ● Purpose of evolution: The First Source and Center has a purpose in creating the universe, and that purpose is the perfecting of will creatures. The universe is evolving toward that purpose, and the First Source and Center, in co-operation with the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit, is leading this process. The Urantia Book likens the relationship between the First Source and Center and the universe to that of a father and his children. The universe is a creation filled with the love and mercy of the First Source and Center, and the will creatures who grow and evolve within it will ultimately return to the Father's embrace.

q016.question: What do the various terms for Deity in the Urantia Papers mean?
q016.answer:
The Urantia Book uses various terms to designate Deity, and each term carries a specific meaning and context. The meanings of the principal terms are as follows.

1. Deity ●Deity is the term with the most comprehensive meaning; it includes not only personal beings but the whole of universe reality, such as impersonal realities, mind meanings, and spirit values. ●Deity exists in ways that transcend human understanding, and it has the attribute of unifying all things in the realms beyond material reality. ●Deity exists in personal, prepersonal, and superpersonal states, and each state is connected with the others.

2. God ●God is the term designating personalized Deity, and in particular it refers to the Universal Father, that is, the Creator, Controller, and Upholder. ●God always denotes a personal being, and its meaning may vary according to various functions and relationships. ●For example, God the Father, God the Son, God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and God the Absolute each denote a different dimension of divinity and function.

3. Divinity ●Divinity means the attribute of Deity that expresses the characteristics of Deity's personality, the unifying and co-ordinating quality of Deity. ●Man can understand divinity through such concepts as truth, beauty, goodness, love, mercy, ministry, justice, power, and sovereignty. ●Divinity may be perfect or imperfect, and it may also have a relative character.

4. The First Source and Center ●The First Source and Center is one of Deity's modes of existence, the fundamental cause of all reality. ●The Universal Father is the personal expression of the First Source and Center and has infinite control over all other sources and centers. ●The First Source and Center is primal in all domains, and all things and beings depend directly or indirectly on the First Source and Center. Through these various terms The Urantia Book explains the various aspects and attributes of Deity and its relationship with the universe and with creatures. Understanding these terms is an important key to grasping the complex concept of Deity in The Urantia Book.

q017.question: What did Pilate fear as he examined Jesus?
q017.answer: In examining Jesus, Pilate seems to have feared the following things. •A Jewish uprising: Pilate was afraid that Jesus' followers might start a riot. Pilate's relations with the Jews were already poor, and he worried that the situation would grow worse because of the matter of Jesus. •His own political standing: Pilate worried that if he released Jesus he would be accused of disloyalty to Caesar. He thought that his political career could be endangered. •Ignorance of truth: Pilate asked Jesus, "What is truth?" but his attitude was not one of truly seeking an answer. •The kingdom of Jesus: When Jesus said that his kingdom was not of this world, Pilate understood that it was not a challenge to Roman power. At the same time, however, he thought that Jesus' claim might be a potential threat to his own authority. (Reference passages) 185:3.3 Then said Jesus to Pilate: "⟦Q 185:3.3⟧“Não percebes que o meu Reino não é deste mundo? Se o meu Reino fosse deste mundo, os meus discípulos certamente lutariam para que eu não fosse entregue nas mãos dos judeus. A minha presença aqui diante de ti, de mãos atadas, é suficiente para mostrar a todos os homens que o meu Reino é um domínio espiritual, como a fraternidade dos homens que se tornaram filhos de Deus, pela fé e pelo amor. E essa salvação é para os gentios, tanto quanto para os judeus”.⟦/Q⟧." 185:3.4 "⟦Q 185:3.4⟧Then you are a king after all?⟦/Q⟧" said Pilate. And Jesus answered: "⟦Q 185:3.4⟧Yes, I am such a king, and my kingdom is the family of the faith sons of my Father who is in heaven. For this purpose was I born into this world, even that I should show my Father to all men and bear witness to the truth of God. And even now do I declare to you that every one who loves the truth hears my voice⟦/Q⟧." 185:3.5 Then said Pilate, half in ridicule and half in sincerity, "⟦Q 185:3.5⟧Truth, what is truth—who knows?⟦/Q⟧"

q018.question: What are the seven levels of Deity function?
q018.answer: Deity can function on the following seven levels. 1.Static level: self-contained and self-existent Deity. 2.Potential level: self-willed and self-purposive Deity. 3.Associative level: self-personalized and divinely fraternal Deity. 4.Creative level: self-distributive and divinely revealed Deity. 5.Evolutional level: self-expansive and creature-identified Deity. 6.Supreme level: self-experiential and creature-Creator-unifying Deity. It is Deity functioning on the first creature-identificational level as time-space overcontroller of the grand universe, and it is sometimes regarded as the Supremacy of Deity. 7.Ultimate level: self-projected and time-space-transcending Deity. It is Deity omnipotent, omniscient, and omnipresent. Deity functioning on the second level of unifying divinity expression as effective overcontroller and absonite upholder of the master universe. As compared with the ministry of the overcontrollers of the grand universe, this absonite function in the master universe is tantamount to universal overcontrol and supersustenance, and it is sometimes called the Ultimacy of Deity. (Reference passages) 0:1.1 The universe of universes presents phenomena of deity activities on diverse levels of cosmic realities, mind meanings, and spirit values, but all of these ministrations—personal or otherwise—are divinely co-ordinated. 0:1.2 DEITY is personalizable as God, is prepersonal and superpersonal in ways not altogether comprehensible by man. Deity is characterized by the quality of unity—actual or potential—on all supermaterial levels of reality; and this unifying quality is best comprehended by creatures as divinity. 0:1.3 Deity functions on personal, prepersonal, and superpersonal levels. Total Deity is functional on the following seven levels: 0:1.4 1. Static—self-contained and self-existent Deity. 0:1.5 2. Potential—self-willed and self-purposive Deity. 0:1.6 3. Associative—self-personalized and divinely fraternal Deity. 0:1.7 4. Creative—self-distributive and divinely revealed Deity. 0:1.8 5. Evolutional—self-expansive and creature-identified Deity. 0:1.9 6. Supreme—self-experiential and creature-Creator-unifying Deity. Deity functioning on the first creature-identificational level as time-space overcontrollers of the grand universe, sometimes designated the Supremacy of Deity. 0:1.10 7. Ultimate—self-projected and time-space-transcending Deity. Deity omnipotent, omniscient, and omnipresent. Deity functioning on the second level of unifying divinity expression as effective overcontrollers and absonite upholders of the master universe. As compared with the ministry of the Deities to the grand universe, this absonite function in the master universe is tantamount to universal overcontrol and supersustenance, sometimes called the Ultimacy of Deity.

q019.question: How is the Paradise Trinity defined and explained in terms of divinity, power, and function?
q019.answer: The Paradise Trinity is defined and explained as follows. •Divinity: The Paradise Trinity consists of the personalities who constitute total Deity. That is, the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit are, in a certain sense, the constituent personalities of total Deity, and their union in the Paradise Trinity and the absolute function of the Trinity are equivalent to the function of total Deity. •Power: The Paradise Trinity transcends both the finite and the absonite. No single person of the Paradise Deities actually fills all Deity potential, but collectively all three do, and three infinite persons seem to be the minimum number of beings required to activate the prepersonal and existential potential of total Deity—the Deity Absolute. •Function: The Paradise Trinity is as one in all universe reality reactions and in all creature relations. The existence of these three external persons does not diminish the truth of the indivisibility of Deity; it implies that time and space are transcended, and neither time nor space is absolute or infinite. The First Source and Center is that infinity who unqualifiedly transcends all mind, all matter, and all spirit. •The Universal Father is called the Infinite Upholder, the Divine Controller, the Father of Lights, the Gift of Life, the All-powerful One, and so on. He never imposes any form of arbitrary name, formal worship, or slavish service upon the intelligent will creatures. •The Eternal Son is the complete and final expression of the "first" personal and absolute concept of the Universal Father. He originates on Paradise and is the center of spirit gravity. •The Infinite Spirit is the universal divine minister; he ministers the mercy of the Son and the love of the Father in harmony with the stable, unchanging, and righteous justice of the Paradise Trinity. In summary, the Paradise Trinity possesses ultimate unity in divinity, power, and function, and the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit function harmoniously, each fulfilling his own unique role. (Reference passages) 10:8.3 The Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit are, in a certain sense, the constituent personalities of total Deity. Their union in the Paradise Trinity and the absolute function of the Trinity equivalate to the function of total Deity. And such completion of Deity transcends both the finite and the absonite. 10:8.4 While no single person of the Paradise Deities actually fills all Deity potential, collectively all three do. Three infinite persons seem to be the minimum number of beings required to activate the prepersonal and existential potential of total Deity—the Deity Absolute. 10:8.5 We know the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit as persons, but I do not personally know the Deity Absolute. I love and worship God the Father; I respect and honor the Deity Absolute. 10:8.6 I once sojourned in a universe where a certain group of beings taught that the finaliters, in eternity, were eventually to become the children of the Deity Absolute. But I am unwilling to accept this solution of the mystery which enshrouds the future of the finaliters. 1:7.7 This concept of indivisibility in association with the concept of unity implies transcendence of both time and space by the Ultimacy of Deity; therefore neither space nor time can be absolute or infinite. The First Source and Center is that infinity who unqualifiedly transcends all mind, all matter, and all spirit. 1:7.8 The fact of the Paradise Trinity in no manner violates the truth of the divine unity. The three personalities of Paradise Deity are, in all universe reality reactions and in all creature relations, as one. Neither does the existence of these three eternal persons violate the truth of the indivisibility of Deity. I am fully aware that I have at my command no language adequate to make clear to the mortal mind how these universe problems appear to us. But you should not become discouraged; not all of these things are wholly clear to even the high personalities belonging to my group of Paradise beings. Ever bear in mind that these profound truths pertaining to Deity will increasingly clarify as your minds become progressively spiritualized during the successive epochs of the long mortal ascent to Paradise.

q020.question: What effects did the Lucifer rebellion have on Urantia and the universe of Nebadon, and how are those effects being overcome?
q020.answer: The Lucifer rebellion had serious effects on Urantia and the universe of Nebadon, and those effects are being overcome through several stages. Effects of the Lucifer rebellion: •The isolation of Urantia: At the time of the Lucifer rebellion, Urantia was isolated because of the Caligastia betrayal. •Interference with Michael's bestowal mission: Lucifer, Satan, and Caligastia joined together in an attempt to thwart Michael's bestowal mission on Urantia. •The delay of justice: Lucifer pointed to the merciful delay of justice as evidence that the government of the Paradise Sons could not stop the rebellion. •The attack on the plan for training ascending mortals: Lucifer opposed the plan of training ascending mortals in the principles of universe administration, claiming that it was unethical and unsound. Overcoming the effects of the Lucifer rebellion: •Michael's victory: When Michael was bestowed in the flesh on Urantia, he withstood and triumphed over the attempts of Lucifer, Satan, and Caligastia. •Gabriel's action: When Michael triumphed, Gabriel came down from Salvington and bound the dragon (all the rebel leaders) for an age. •Norlatiadek: Since the triumph of Christ, all Norlatiadek is being cleansed of sin and rebels. •The efforts of the angelic hosts: The angelic hosts were instructed to work for the full disclosure of sin and for unlimited opportunity to confess it, as the quickest technique of achieving the full and final cure of the plague of evil and sin. •The counsel of the Solitary Messengers: An emergency council of ex-mortals, made up of Solitary Messengers with personal experience, advised Gabriel that if arbitrary or makeshift suppression were attempted, at least three times as many beings would be led astray. •The passing of time: The whole Uversa advisory corps advised Gabriel to allow the rebellion to run its full and natural course, even if it should take a million years for the consequences of the rebellion to come to an end. •The restoration of the system: Andovontia expresses pleasure to the mortals of Urantia in the anticipation of their sometime restoration to the universe circuits of his supervision. •The age of light and life: When the Trinity Teacher Sons complete their final mission and depart, the age of light and life will be inaugurated. The Lucifer rebellion was an infringement upon the free-will choice of the ascenders and ministers of the system of Satania, and a threat to deprive them of the opportunity to contribute their experiential wisdom. However, through Michael's victory and the process of universe healing, the universe of Nebadon is gradually being freed from the effects of the rebellion, and Urantia too is moving toward the age of light and life. (Reference passages) 53:1.4 Very little was heard of Lucifer on Urantia owing to the fact that he assigned his first lieutenant, Satan, to advocate his cause on your planet. Satan was a member of the same primary group of Lanonandeks but had never functioned as a System Sovereign; he entered fully into the Lucifer insurrection. The "devil" is none other than Caligastia, the deposed Planetary Prince of Urantia and a Son of the secondary order of Lanonandeks. At the time Michael was on Urantia in the flesh, Lucifer, Satan, and Caligastia were leagued together to effect the miscarriage of his bestowal mission. But they signally failed. 37:8.2 (413.5) ⟦P 37:8.2⟧ 37:8.3 (413.6) ⟦P 37:8.3⟧

q021.question: What role and relationship does the Mother Spirit have with the Creator Son in the local universe, and how does she influence their children?
q021.answer: The Creator Son (Michael) and the Mother Spirit (the Divine Minister, the Creative Spirit) have a very close and essential role and relationship in the local universe, and they exert wide-ranging influence on their children, the creatures of the local universe. The role and relationships of the Mother Spirit: •Personalization of the Infinite Spirit: The Creative Mother Spirit of the local universe is the personalized presence of the Infinite Spirit and is known in Satania as the Divine Minister. As a spirit person she is recognized and regarded as such by the Creator Son. •Subordination to the Creator Son: Through the localization and personalization of the Third Source and Center in the local universe, the Spirit could become fully subject to the Creator Son, and thus the saying "⟦Q 34:1.4⟧All power in heaven and on earth has been intrusted to him⟦/Q⟧" became true. •Co-worker in the creative enterprise: The Divine Minister, having undergone marked personality metamorphosis at the time of life creation, co-operates in a very personal manner with the Creator Son in planning and managing the extensive affairs of the local creation. •Possession of the attributes of the Infinite Spirit: From the earliest association with the Creator Son, the Universe Spirit possesses all the physical-control attributes of the Infinite Spirit, including the full endowment of antigravity, and after attaining personal status she exerts full and complete control of mind gravity. •Imparting and sustaining life: The Creative Spirit is jointly responsible with the Creator Son for creating the creatures of the worlds, and she never fails the Son in all his efforts to guard and preserve these creations. Life is fostered and sustained through the agencies of the Creative Spirit. •The spark of life and the endowment of mind: The Life Carriers can organize material forms, but the Spirit provides the initial spark of life and bestows the endowment of mind. The animal mind and the human mind are gifts of the local universe Mother Spirit, functioning through the seven adjutant mind-spirits. •Bestowal of reproductive ability: The biologic ability to reproduce is the specific and personal implantation by the Universe Spirit in the primordial protoplasm initiated by the Life Carriers. •Influence after death: The life imparted to plants and animals does not return to the Life Carriers at death but survives only as part of the cosmic forces of the universe, whereas the survival of mortal creatures depends on the evolution of an immortal soul within the human mind. •Source of spiritual power: The divine Spirit is the source of continual ministry and encouragement to the children of men. Our power and achievement is "⟦Q 34:6.5⟧according to his mercy, through the renewing of the Spirit⟦/Q⟧." •Giving life to truth: Until the divine Spirit indwells the form of truth and gives life to the doctrines of righteousness, the seed of theoretical truth is dead, and the highest moral concepts are without effect. Influence on the children: •Source of life and mind: The Creator Son and the Mother Spirit jointly create all intelligent life in the local universe, and the Mother Spirit in particular bestows on them the spark of life and the endowment of mind. •Nurture and preservation: The life that has been created is fostered and sustained through the agencies of the Mother Spirit. •Support for spiritual growth: The divine Spirit provides continual ministry and encouragement to the children of men and helps their spiritual growth and development. • Regeneration and resurrection: The Mother Spirit takes part in the process by which deceased mortals are resurrected in morontia form. •Guidance in truth and righteousness: The Holy Spirit indwells truth and gives life to the doctrines of righteousness, helping mortals to gain spiritual understanding. In summary, the Creator Son, as sovereign and chief executive of the local universe, is responsible for its overall administration and government, while the Mother Spirit, as the source of life and the creative partner who bestows mind, plays an essential role in the existence and development of all living things. Working closely together, they create and sustain the local universe and are like loving and capable parents who provide their children with opportunities for life, mind, and spiritual growth. (Reference passages) 34:1.4 (375.3) ⟦P 34:1.4⟧ 34:2.1 (375.4) ⟦P 34:2.1⟧ 34:2.2 (375.5) ⟦P 34:2.2⟧

q022.question: How does the Thought Adjuster contribute to the spiritual development of mortal man?
q022.answer:
The Thought Adjuster contributes profoundly to the spiritual development of mortal man in several ways, as follows. •The presence of divinity and connection with it: The Thought Adjuster is the gift of the Universal Father and the reflection of the image of God within man. This gives man the potential to be connected with a divine source beyond merely material existence. The Adjuster is the hope of divine character within man and provides the power, privilege, and possibility of survival that forever distinguish man from mere animal existence. •Inner spiritual stimulus: In contrast with external material stimulus, the Adjuster is the truly internal spiritual stimulus arising in human thought. It leads man beyond material desires and impulses to pursue higher spiritual values and goals. •Spiritual re-creation and the evolution of the soul: The Thought Adjuster transforms every mental creation into a spiritual counterpart, and thus is slowly and surely actually re-creating man. These spiritual re-creations are preserved in the new reality of the evolving and immortal soul, the morontia self. Even though the Adjuster is sometimes unable to exhibit these creations sufficiently to the light of consciousness, these realities actually exist and become the foundation of spiritual growth. The Adjuster is like the divine parent of man's evolving immortal soul. •The driving force of eternal progress: The Adjuster unceasingly urges man to go beyond present material existence and pursue the spiritual and future higher career. They are the prisoners of undying hope and the founts of everlasting progression, encouraging man never to stop growing spiritually but to progress unceasingly. •Flashes of truth and guidance: The Thought Adjuster strives to transmit new flashes of truth to the evolving mortal soul. Although such spiritual revelations sometimes come to man overwhelmingly and may give rise to misunderstanding, the Adjuster ceaselessly seeks to raise man's understanding and to give spiritual enlightenment. When man is able to recognize the leading of the Monitor, the Adjuster strives to make known what is truly right. •Preservation of values: The Thought Adjuster never fails, and nothing worthy of survival is ever lost. Even if a man rejects survival, the valuable elements of his life experience are preserved by the Adjuster and may be bestowed on a higher type of human mind on another world. This means that all of man's meaningful values are preserved forever. •Ultimate fusion and union with God: On worlds such as Urantia a true betrothal with the Thought Adjuster takes place, and if man survives there will be eternal fusion, in which man and Adjuster become one. The man who co-operates with the Adjuster eventually evolves into an immortal morontia soul, and after fusion with the Adjuster this new creature will be presented to the Universal Father. In summary, the Thought Adjuster, as the spark of divinity indwelling man, provides unceasing spiritual stimulus and guidance, evolves the immortal soul, and plays the central role in leading man ultimately to union with God. Man's spiritual growth depends on his co-operation with the Adjuster and his effort to follow the inner leading. (Reference passages) 108:6.3 The Mystery Monitors are undoubtedly the bestowal of the Universal Father, the reflection of the image of God abroad in the universe. A great teacher once admonished men that they should be renewed in the spirit of their minds; that they become new men who, like God, are created in righteousness and in the completion of truth. The Adjuster is the mark of divinity, the presence of God. The "image of God" does not refer to physical likeness nor to the circumscribed limitations of material creature endowment but rather to the gift of the spirit presence of the Universal Father in the supernal bestowal of the Thought Adjusters upon the humble creatures of the universes. 108:6.4 The Adjuster is the wellspring of spiritual attainment and the hope of divine character within you. He is the power, privilege, and the possibility of survival, which so fully and forever distinguishes you from mere animal creatures. He is the higher and truly internal spiritual stimulus of thought in contrast with the external and physical stimulus, which reaches the mind over the nerve-energy mechanism of the material body. 108:6.5 These faithful custodians of the future career unfailingly duplicate every mental creation with a spiritual counterpart; they are thus slowly and surely re-creating you as you really are (only spiritually) for resurrection on the survival worlds. And all of these exquisite spirit re-creations are being preserved in the emerging reality of your evolving and immortal soul, your morontia self. These realities are actually there, notwithstanding that the Adjuster is seldom able to exalt these duplicate creations sufficiently to exhibit them to the light of consciousness.

108:6.6 And as you are the human parent, so is the Adjuster the divine parent of the real you, your higher and advancing self, your better morontial and future spiritual self. And it is this evolving morontial soul that the judges and censors discern when they decree your survival and pass you upward to new worlds and never-ending existence in eternal liaison with your faithful partner—God, the Adjuster. 108:6.7 The Adjusters are the eternal ancestors, the divine originals, of your evolving immortal souls; they are the unceasing urge that leads man to attempt the mastery of the material and present existence in the light of the spiritual and future career. The Monitors are the prisoners of undying hope, the founts of everlasting progression. And how they do enjoy communicating with their subjects in more or less direct channels!
