How they rejoice when they can dispense with symbols and other methods of indirection and flash their messages straight to the intellects of their human partners! 108:6.8 You humans have begun an endless unfolding of an almost infinite panorama, a limitless expanding of never-ending, ever-widening spheres of opportunity for exhilarating service, matchless adventure, sublime uncertainty, and boundless attainment. When the clouds gather overhead, your faith should accept the fact of the presence of the indwelling Adjuster, and thus you should be able to look beyond the mists of mortal uncertainty into the clear shining of the sun of eternal righteousness on the beckoning heights of the mansion worlds of Satania.

q023.question: How did Jesus' human growth and experience, from his early life until the beginning of his public ministry, influence the carrying out of his mission?
q023.answer: Jesus' human growth and experience, from his early life until the beginning of his public ministry, influenced the carrying out of his mission in many ways. This influence appears clearly in his teachings, his understanding of man, and his manner of ministry. •Responsibility for and devotion to his family: Growing up in Nazareth, after the sudden death of his father Jesus took on the responsibility of supporting the family as its head. He devoted himself to his mother and his eight brothers and sisters, and he adhered to the terms of his plea, stressing that they needed a father's watchcare and guidance, something more than material things. Making his memorable statement that "money cannot love," he put his duty to his family first. This experience probably influenced the emphasis on the importance of love and devotion in his teachings. It may also have become the basis for his deep understanding of human bonds and the value of community. •Experiences in the temple and intellectual inquiry: As a boy, Jesus stayed in the temple with the teachers, discussing the law and asking questions. On the third day in the temple his questions drew the attention of the scribes, and one of them was, "⟦Q 125:5.3⟧O que realmente existe no santo dos santos, atrás do véu?⟦/Q⟧" This early intellectual curiosity and probing questioning probably became the source of his ability, during his ministry, to challenge authoritative religious leaders and to explore spiritual truth. •Association with many kinds of people and the capacity for sympathy: Experiences such as befriending Gadiah, the Philistine interpreter who worked for Simon the tanner in Joppa, his conversation with Anaxand, the young Greek working in the shipyard, and his conversations with Ganid about the workings of the human mind as they traveled together gave Jesus a broad outlook for communicating with people of various cultures and backgrounds and for understanding their lives and anguish. In particular, his encouraging Anaxand to overcome evil with the power of good, and his teaching Ganid that to one who knows God there are no strangers, show his embracing love and understanding. These experiences were probably an important foundation for his ability, during his public life, to approach people of every class, sympathize with their needs, and teach them. •Personal spiritual discipline and solitude: After the second day in the temple was over, Jesus went to Bethany to spend the night, and again went out into the garden to meditate and pray. Also, during the six weeks spent on Mount Hermon, he finished the tasks of mind understanding and personality control and took time to commune with the Father in heaven. Such deep spiritual discipline and meditation in solitude probably played a decisive role in strengthening his inner life, discerning the will of God, and clearly recognizing his mission. In particular, the experience of being permitted to bear alone the final struggle with the realities of mortal existence probably contributed to forming his inner strength and spiritual authority. •Restraint toward the temptation of miracles: At the wedding feast at Cana, when his mother Mary asked him to manifest himself by working a miracle, Jesus answered firmly, "⟦Q 137:4.4⟧“Se me amais, então estejais dispostos a permanecer comigo, enquanto espero pela vontade do meu Pai que está nos céus”.⟦/Q⟧," showing his determination not to display his divinity lightly. This suggests that he clearly recognized that his mission was not simply to work miracles but to follow the will of the Father in heaven and to proclaim spiritual truth. These various experiences of his early life formed the foundation of the love, devotion, wisdom, capacity for sympathy, spiritual authority, and firm determination regarding his mission that Jesus showed during his public life. His human growth had a deep and lasting influence on the carrying out of his mission, and it became the foundation for conveying an eternal message to mankind through his teachings and deeds.

q024.question: Why do the seven orders of Supreme Trinity Personalities exist?
q024.answer:
The Supreme Trinity Personalities are all created for specific service. The divine Trinity designed them for the fulfillment of certain specific duties, and they are qualified to render this service. They represent the administrative policies of the Paradise Trinity throughout the grand universe. They represent justice and are the executive judgment of the Paradise Trinity. They form an interrelated and perfect line of administration from the Paradise spheres of the Father to the headquarters worlds of the local universes and to the capitals of the constellations. These beings are all of Trinity origin and were created with Paradise perfection and all the divine attributes. There is never any danger of their failure or possibility of their rebellion, and this ensures their reliability in serving and administering. To their preparation for universe service has been added the passing of time in the realms of experience. The different orders of Supreme Trinity Personalities accomplish this overall purpose by carrying out specific administrative and advisory roles on the various levels of the universe. For example:

1. Trinitized Secrets of Supremacy: the supreme-ultimate administrators who preside over the seven sacred spheres near Paradise. Their work has to do with the personal relations of the Deities with universe beings.

2. Eternals of Days: they supervise each of the one billion worlds of Havona. They are visible to all will creatures in their realms and preside over the regular planetary conclaves.

3. Ancients of Days: the high spiritual rulers and directors who head the administration of the seven superuniverses. They impose uniform administration in the midst of the creative diversity of the superuniverses and ensure the harmony of the whole. They are the most powerful rulers in the universes of time and space, with authority to pronounce the final executive verdict concerning the eternal extinction of will creatures. In the present age, while the Supreme Being is attaining sovereignty as experiential sovereign, they provide the evolving universes with co-ordinated and perfect overall control.

4. Perfections of Days: they preside over the governments of the major sectors of each superuniverse and were brought into being to assist the superuniverse rulers. They rule as the immediate vicegerents of the Ancients of Days. In the major sectors they are closely associated with the higher training of the ascending mortals from the worlds of time.

5. Recents of Days: the superuniverse directors who preside over the affairs of the minor sectors. Their administrative authority is subordinate to the higher orders, and they are concerned with the major physical problems of the superuniverse.

6. Unions of Days: advisers and counselors who act as representatives of the Paradise Trinity in the local universes. They co-ordinate the administrative activities of all branches of universe government, which is the reason for their name. They act at the request of the local authorities and are fundamentally Trinity ambassadors and Paradise counselors.

7. Faithfuls of Days: Paradise counselors who advise the rulers governing the constellations of each local universe. They are supremely devoted to the welfare of the constellations to which they are assigned, and they act only as counselors. They are under the jurisdiction of the Union of Days of the local universe. In summary, the seven orders of Supreme Trinity Personalities were created to carry out the specific duties and services of the divine Trinity, to represent the administrative policies, justice, and executive judgment of the Paradise Trinity throughout the grand universe, and to form a perfect and interrelated line of administration of universe government. They perform a wide range of administrative roles, such as ruling, co-ordinating, counseling, and training, on the various levels of the universe.
